history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Maitri Bagh ('Garden of Friendship') is a zoo-cum-children's park at Maroda Sector, Bhilai, established as a symbol of India-Soviet friendship and developed/maintained by the Bhilai Steel Plant (SAIL). Sources conflict on founding: Wikipedia/Central Zoo Authority say established 1972; Dainik Jagran reports the garden was founded in 1965 and converted into a zoo in 1972. It is Chhattisgarh's largest and oldest zoo, a noted white-tiger conservation centre (first pair from Nandankanan arrived 1990; 19 white tigers born since). Attractions include the artificial lake with boating, musical fountain, toy train, and memorials of the Soviet-era collaboration. No temple is documented within or as the site; the CSV row appears to name the park itself. PROBABLE DUPLICATE: CSV seq 179 ('Maitri Bagh Temple, Bhilai', handled by another worker) refers to the same site - 179's town (Bhilai) is correct; this row's town 'Durg' is the district name. Town corrected to Bhilai.

name: Maitri Bagh Zoo (Garden of Friendship)
town_description: Bhilai is an industrial city in Durg district, Chhattisgarh, built around the Bhilai Steel Plant (commissioned 1959 with Soviet collaboration); its planned sectors and township host numerous temples serving the steel-town population.
tradition: Non-religious - zoological park and public garden

travel.railway: Durg Junction on the Mumbai-Howrah main line; nearest station Bhilai Power House
travel.road: Maroda Sector, Bhilai (~9 km from Durg district HQ)
